- If sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to account for bearish momentum reversal.
- If sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is rising, model often overestimates; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment swings sharply upward after a dip, model frequently fails to capture the lagged rebound; delay peak forecast by 1–2 days and smooth upward slope.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in early days of a 30d window, it’s overconfident; apply downward bias of 1–3% for first 5–7 days.
- If true price spikes >10% from recent mean, model often fails to catch it; add a 2–5% upward adjustment to forecast if sentiment is positive and volatility is high.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply smoothing or reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid false peaks.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is >15% above 14d moving average, model often underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for the first 10 days of the horizon.
